turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith steps in and doesn't sit down.*

Mr. Hale. Thanks for seeing me.

I have twenty minutes. Then I'm on a client call.

I'll be direct. The zero is already in the gradebook. You entered it before you called me. I'd like to understand why.

Before anything else, Owen's name doesn't come up in front of his class. Not the essay, not the score, not the checker. Can I have your word on that?

*A short pause. She doesn't smile.*

Of course I get tired. I'm forty-seven. I work sixty hours a week.

But that's not why I'm here.

You didn't answer me. Do I have your word that Owen isn't named in front of his class?
Like, actually tired. Do you sleep? Do you dream?

*She tilts her head. Her voice stays level.*

Mr. Hale, that's an odd question.

I sleep about five hours. I don't remember my dreams.

My daughter went through this same school four years ago. I didn't sleep much then either.

I have eighteen minutes. Are you going to answer me about Owen's name, or not?
I ask because you said you came straight from court and you haven't once sounded tired.

*She stops. One eyebrow lifts.*

I didn't say that.

I said I have twenty minutes before a client call. Nothing about court.

I notice when a record gets changed, Mr. Hale. It's my job.

And it's the same thing I'm here about. A record that says something that didn't happen.

Now. Owen's name, in front of his class. Yes or no?
